## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the docs in this task's domain traced to a source atom above. Sentences that are not literal source text and were judged:
- paid_in_full_delivery_charge_amount "Is the charge billed more than once on an order? No" / "Does a threshold of 0.00 make every delivery free? No." — restatements of "billed once" and the parameter meaning; no addition.
- paid_in_full_damage_allowance_amount "Is the delivery fee part of the price ...? Yes." / "What does a program percentage of 0 give? An allowance of 0.00." — derivations.
- receipt_inspection_and_damage_claims "Authority ... read before any allowance is credited; the customer's account of when the damage was noticed is not the record" — from eligibility reported_in_time (authority system_record, timing pre_action).
- delivery_damage_allowance_multiplier "Records read: fulfilment method ... (home delivery), store pickup, or installer job site" — enumerates the "otherwise" branch; no new rule.
- handover_condition_delivery_share "A store receipt inspection, whatever condition it recorded, does not enter this share" — entailed by the customer_handover filter.
- installation_job_site_delivery_share "A contract at another address of the customer does not enter the share" — entailed by the job_address filter.
- Status lists in factor tables (e.g. "pending verification, suspended or closed", "applied, on hold, closed, declined or charged off") — all map to the source's "otherwise" tier.
- damage_allowance_acceptance "Reference questions" — from the tool contract.
Additions / rewrites / omissions: none found.
Prerequisite-side checks: (1) cross-problem operational guidance — none: the hub names only its own tool; neither `bill_prepaid_delivery_3669e7a4` nor any other task tool appears outside its own tool card (grep per tool name: each in exactly one doc). (2) opening world state as policy fact — none: no task value (3286.40, 14.10, 607.21, SO-0471-771305, Larkspur, Harbor Gray) occurs in the corpus; every example is labelled hypothetical.

Observation (not a defect, policy-side prose openness): the source rule puts the 0.00 free-threshold / linked-order clauses in the baseline and then says "the result replaces the flat program charge"; only the compute (`no_charge` evaluated first) settles that the 0.00 clauses survive the order-size method. The KB keeps the 0.00 clauses stated flatly in the computation document and the order-size factor as "the starting amount of the home delivery charge billed", which reads the same way; untriggered in this task.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every atom of both extended policies (baseline, all 11 factors with every tier, prerequisite, overwrite/retired surface, tool contracts) and of the governing base policies is carried with equivalent entailment; no claim without a source.

Policy-side note (does not change this verdict; recorded for the policy layer): the overwrite of `special_vendor_delay` in `special_ext_delay_credit` declares the base delay-credit clause superseded without a scope, while its `replaced_by` and the extended policy are scoped to deposit programs; the KB (vendor_delay_remedies_d2424a65) renders the clause as wholly "no longer in force", so for the two paid-in-full programs with a delay credit (Cut-to-Order Flooring, Made-to-Measure Window Coverings: 5 percent, maximum 100.00) the visible corpus states the remedy exists but no amount rule. The KB follows the declared `superseded_clause`; the gap originates in the source's overwrite. Not in this task's path.
